chapters.narrative: City-wide basement is reported as Peninsular Gneissic Complex of Archean age 2500-3500 mya, with Closepet granite averaging 4 km width and Gabbro-Dolerite-Norite-Pyroxenite intrusions marking Lower Proterozoic transition. Metro Phase 3 documentation independently places corridors in the same PGC on Deccan Plateau at 850-950 m elevation. No site-specific bedrock depths or RQD values are supplied beyond this lithologic framing.
chapters.summary: Archean PGC basement with Closepet granite and basic intrusions underlies 711 sq km BBMP at 850-950 m.
chapters.title: Bedrock geology

chapters.narrative: Dominant cover is 2-4 m red lateritic soil over saprolite with 2.4-8.2 cm/hr infiltration in 8 Red Soil tests. Metro geotechnics describe 0-10 m cohesionless soil with gravels/cobbles over moderately strong to strong granite-gneiss-migmatite, with >10 m soil in BH02-BH04 and BH22-BH26. South Indian SoilGrid Bulletin identity is listed but no grid values are extracted.
chapters.summary: Red laterite 2-4 m with moderate infiltration over 0-10 m cohesionless overburden on PGC.
chapters.title: Soil and overburden

chapters.narrative: Two-tier system is source-stated: Aquifer-I phreatic weathered zone over Aquifer-II semi-confined to confined fractured zone. Median weathered depth 19.35 m IQR 10-30 m is city-wide statistic. Fracture census shows 52% in 50-100 m bgl as most productive interval. GSI Campus cluster demonstrates short-space heterogeneity with deep EW fracture at 195-196 m versus shallow OW1 fracture at 22-23 m.
chapters.summary: Phreatic weathered aquifer over fractured aquifer with 50-100 m productive zone and local heterogeneity.
chapters.title: Aquifer architecture

chapters.narrative: 2023 drought showed 4.1-85.5 m pre to 3.19-92.6 m post with 84.1% falls; 2024 showed 2.51-163.51 m pre to 2.00-135.15 m post with 72.04% rises. GWRA 2024 stage 242.08% overexploited with recharge 91.89 MCM versus extraction 200.21 MCM. Demand 2676 MLD versus supply 1893 MLD leaves 783 MLD deficit met partly by 746 MLD groundwater and tankers. Derived 238 sq km eastern-southeastern scarcity zone with >50 m post-monsoon and/or >5 m fall covers 52 wards.
chapters.summary: Drought-sensitive levels, 242% overexploitation, 783 MLD deficit and 238 sq km scarcity zone.
chapters.title: Water levels and budget stress

chapters.narrative: Phase 3 comprises Corridor 3-1 32.15 km 22 stations and Corridor 3-2 12.50 km 9 stations, fully elevated double-decker viaduct, schematic only without georeferenced alignment. 36 boreholes to 30 m at ~1000 m spacing support pile foundations except BH12/16 raft on shallow rock. Seismic Zone II low intensity per BIS IS 1893:2002 is preserved with conflicting Zone III statement unresolved.
chapters.summary: Two fully elevated double-decker corridors on PGC requiring pier-specific investigation.
chapters.title: Metro infrastructure and foundations

chapters.narrative: BWSSB KML network registers 97827 features with 95138 LineString and 2689 None geometry; samples have empty name/description and no hydraulic attributes. Network is referenced for supply versus borewell dependence and for siting recharge, not bulk-copied. Lake cascade Series A 1.07 plus Series B 1.90 totals 2.97 MCM/year recharge at 1.44 mm/day is small relative to ~108 MCM deficit.
chapters.summary: 97827-feature piped network referenced without hydraulics; lake cascade offers limited recharge.
chapters.title: Water-supply network and recharge

chapters.narrative: Line 3-2 southern end is 7.05 km table /7.1 km text from Bannerghatta National Park, nearest protected area with no direct overlap. Scarcity, deep levels, thick weathered cover, high yield and partial Cauvery coverage co-locate in east-southeast. Quality shows nitrate to 608.59 mg/L and uranium to 1109.6 ppb exceeding 30 ppb in 35-45% samples with Mn, Se, F exceedances, constraining reuse for lake filling without treatment.
chapters.summary: 7.05 km park separation; eastern scarcity-quality coincidence limits untreated recharge.
chapters.title: Spatial relationships and contamination risks

chapters.narrative: Tritium tests at T.C. Palya and GSI sites, 36 metro boreholes to 30 m, 110 levels and soil infiltration tests provide direct basis, but KML has 2689 null geometries and no diameters, metro alignments are schematic, aquifer/soil-grid PDFs lack extracted text, and 2023 drought biases trends. Pier-specific drilling, utility detour surveys and fluoride/uranium compliance remain pending.
chapters.summary: Methods are documented but KML gaps, schematic alignments and missing PDF text limit modeling.
chapters.title: Methods, limitations and unresolved gaps

limitations: KML 2689 of 97827 features have None geometry and samples carry empty name/description; no pipe diameter material age or flow attributes supplied
Metro alignments are schematic only; 36 boreholes to 30 m pending pier-specific and utility detour surveys for detailed design
No extractable text for aquifer, soil-grid and env-impact PDFs beyond listed renders; bedrock depths, yields and grid values not evidenced
2023 was drought year 686 mm vs 976 mm normal; post-monsoon declines partly reflect rainfall not only extraction
Fluoride uranium in treated sewage requires compliance before lake filling; reject-water disposal constrains RO
Borehole coordinates without stated CRS; BWSSB bulk coordinates not copied per methodology
coverage.summary: 22 cited source locators across 711 sq km BBMP; 14 features, 8 intervals, 20 observations and 1 vector dataset support 12 findings; schematic and null-geometry limits preserved.

executive_overview.abstract: Evidence-grounded Bengaluru synthesis for 711 sq km BBMP on Peninsular Gneissic Complex with two-tier aquifer (phreatic median 19.35 m, fractured productive 50-100 m), red laterite 2.4-8.2 cm/hr, 242% overexploitation with 238 sq km eastern scarcity and 783 MLD deficit, 97827-feature BWSSB network referenced without hydraulics, Phase 3 double-decker corridors on piles, Zone II seismic, Bannerghatta 7.05 km away, and 2.97 MCM/year lake recharge. Source-stated values are distinguished from cross-source stress linkages; schematic and data-gap limits are retained.
executive_overview.headline: Overexploited granitic aquifer city with partial piped cover stresses east and constrains metro and recharge planning

findings.statement: Bengaluru City BBMP 12.833-13.142 N 77.462-77.786 E 711 sq km sits on Peninsular Gneissic Complex Archean 2500-3500 mya with Closepet granite avg 4 km width and Gabbro-Dolerite-Norite-Pyroxenite intrusions.
findings.title: Peninsular Gneissic basement
findings.why_it_matters: Hard dense basement controls weathering, fracturing, groundwater regime and metro foundation conditions.

findings.statement: Groundwater occurs as Aquifer-I phreatic weathered zone over Aquifer-II semi-confined to confined fractured zone; urban depth to water 1-5 m bgl.
findings.title: Two-tier aquifer system
findings.why_it_matters: Defines shallow versus deep drilling targets and vulnerability to dewatering and contamination.

findings.statement: Weathered depth median 19.35 m IQR 10-30 m range 1.15-58.4 m with outliers to 76.2 m; mean 21.82 m.
findings.title: Weathered zone thickness
findings.why_it_matters: Constrains shallow aquifer storage and overburden for foundations and recharge siting.

findings.statement: Fractures distribute 0-50 m 30%, 50-100 m 52%, 100-150 m 13%, 150-200 m 5%; 50-100 m is most productive groundwater zone.
findings.title: Fractured productive interval
findings.why_it_matters: Focuses deep borewell targeting and explains eastern high-yield zones.

findings.statement: GSI Campus Kumaraswamy Layout cluster at 12.9108 N 77.5679 E shows EW deep fractured versus OW1 shallow fractured with common source EW-OW2 per borehole camera; rose trends N-S versus NW-SE within short space.
findings.title: GSI drilling heterogeneity
findings.why_it_matters: Demonstrates fracture connectivity cannot be interpolated between close wells for metro dewatering or yield prediction.

findings.title: Water-level drought versus normal year
findings.why_it_matters: Separates climatic drought effect from long-term extraction trend for scarcity delineation.

findings.statement: GWRA 2024 extraction stage 242.08% overexploited with recharge 91.89 MCM versus extraction 200.21 MCM and city deficit 783 MLD coincides with 238 sq km eastern-southeastern scarcity zone with >50 m post-monsoon and/or >5 m fall across 52 wards partly lacking full Cauvery cover.
findings.title: Overexploitation and scarcity linkage
findings.why_it_matters: Links partial piped coverage and borewell dependence to prioritized management and metro water-risk zones.

findings.statement: BWSSB water supply lines KML holds 97827 features with 95138 LineString and 2689 None geometry; samples have empty name/description and no hydraulic attributes; city supply combines Cauvery 1450 plus groundwater 746 plus Stage-V 300 MLD with 705 MLD losses.
findings.title: BWSSB network extent and limits
findings.why_it_matters: Provides spatial reference for utility conflicts and supply gaps but cannot support hydraulic modeling without attributes.

findings.statement: Red laterite soil 2-4 m thick shows infiltration 2.4-8.2 cm/hr across Red Soil sites; Varthur 8.2 highest and Doddabidarekallu 2.4 lowest.
findings.title: Red soil infiltration
findings.why_it_matters: Informs recharge suitability and runoff versus percolation for lake and defunct-well interventions.

findings.statement: Phase 3 Corridor 3-1 32.15 km 22 stations and Corridor 3-2 12.50 km 9 stations fully elevated double-decker are founded in PGC with typical 0-10 m soil over moderately strong to strong rock; 36 boreholes to 30 m support piles except BH12/16 raft; Seismic Zone II low intensity preserved with conflicting Zone III statement.
findings.title: Metro corridors on PGC
findings.why_it_matters: Requires pier-specific drilling and utility trial pits where utilities conflict with piers.

findings.statement: Bannerghatta National Park approx 260.51 sq km is 7.05 km table /7.1 km text from Line 3-2 southern end, nearest protected area with no direct overlap.
findings.title: Protected-area separation
findings.why_it_matters: Screens out direct park impact while retaining urban tree and lake ecological constraints.

findings.statement: Nitrate to 608.59 mg/L and uranium to 1109.6 ppb exceeding 30 ppb in 35-45% samples with Mn Se F exceedances constrain use of secondary treated water; cascading lakes Series A 1.07 plus Series B 1.90 total 2.97 MCM/year at 1.44 mm/day only partly offsets deficit.
findings.title: Quality exceedances and limited lake recharge
findings.why_it_matters: Requires treatment and compliance before lake filling and limits recharge contribution to budget closure.

findings.statement: Tritium sites at T.C. Palya and GSI, 36 metro boreholes and 8 infiltration tests provide direct basis, but 2689 null geometries, schematic metro alignments, and unextracted aquifer/soil-grid PDFs prevent 3D modeling and bulk hydraulic analysis.
findings.title: Methods and unresolved gaps
findings.why_it_matters: Directs detailed-design drilling, GPR/trial trenching and source-text extraction before quantitative modeling.

themes.title: Hydrogeology and water balance

uncertainties.statement: Seismic Zone II low intensity versus Zone III moderate risk statement preserved without reconciliation; design basis pending.
Pipe diameters, materials, depths, pressures and connectivity unknown; 2689 null geometries prevent hydraulic or clash analysis.
238 sq km scarcity interpolated from 93 borewells; ward polygons and Cauvery partial-cover boundaries lack numeric GIS.
2023 drought rainfall 29% deficient biases post-monsoon falls; long-term extraction trend requires DWLR time-series verification.
Nitrate, uranium, Mn, Se, F exceedances and STP fluoride/uranium require treatment verification before lake filling; RO reject disposal unresolved.
Pier-specific geology, utility depths, ramp topography and DDC span redesign remain for detailed design.
Aquifer, soil-grid and env-impact PDFs list renders but supply no extractable text for yields, grid values or EIA baselines.
